title: Onramp Bridgehead — Checklist and Decisions (Customer Pilot)
summary: Working checklist and decision log for a three-stage onramp (hosted -> dedicated -> private) using a temporary 'bridgehead' layer to smooth traffic, validate model variants, and enable incremental operational handoff for a mid-market customer pilot.
body:
Context:
This doc captures our runbook-style checklist, unresolved tradeoffs, and action items for the proposed customer onramp that starts on Redwood hosted, migrates to Dedicated reserved pools, and finally to Private (VPC) with a small bridgehead proxy layer during transitions. Customer: Acme Retail (demo pilot). Primary goals: predictable latency < 150ms tail for chat flows, cost under $X per 1k tokens (see cost sketch), and proof of private connectivity for compliance review.

High-level approach (three stages):
1) Stage A — Hosted (fast start): short-lived hosted deployment with pinned model variant, traffic shaping to limit concurrent KV-heavy sessions. Use streaming responses to keep client perceived latency low. Purpose: validate prompts, gather QoE metrics and token profile.
2) Stage B — Bridgehead + Dedicated (onramp): introduce a lightweight bridgehead (reverse-proxy + routing logic) in the customer region that can route percent-splits between Hosted and Dedicated capacity. Dedicated reserved pool sized for steady-state at 60–80% of peak measured in Stage A; hosted handles spikes and fallback. Purpose: measure cost SLOs and run A/B model comparisons in production.
3) Stage C — Private cutover: after successful canaries and compliance signoff, flip routing in bridgehead to route 100% to Private (customer VPC / on-prem). Bridgehead remains for 30 days as fallback and observability aggregator, then decommissioned.

Design details and rationale:
- Bridgehead responsibilities: TLS termination (optional), request routing by policy (latency-first, cost-first, version pinning), short-term KV cache for prefix reuse, and metrics forwarding (per-token counts, latencies, model variant tag). Keep it stateless wrt long-term KV caches; primary KV caching remains at serving runtime.
- Routing policy examples: initial split 90/10 hosted/dedicated for burst protection, then 50/50 during load tests, then 10/90 before cutover. Automatic circuit-breaker rules: if Dedicated tail latency > 2x baseline OR error rate > 1%, divert 100% to hosted for a rolling 60s window.
- Security posture: bridgehead sits in a Redwood-managed subnet during Stage B with strict egress rules to customer VPC endpoints; mutual TLS for control plane, and optional customer-supplied CA for TLS. Document KMS key access window for Private onboarding (temporary read-only role for onboarding).
- Observability: collect per-request attributes (model hash, token counts, route, response time), ship to Redwood Console and customer SIEM (via syslog/forwarder). Create specific dashboards: "bridgehead-routing", "stage-B-latency-split", "model-regression-spotter".

Capacity and cost sketch (ballpark):
- Expected pilot traffic: 120k tokens/day, average request 600 tokens, peak concurrent requests ~8 rps.
- Dedicated reservation recommendation: 1 x A100-equivalent instance pool with autoscaling headroom + burst pool (short hourly credits) — targeted commit 0.5–1 vGPU-hour/day initial (refine after Stage A metrics).
- Cost-control levers: reduce sequence length via truncation policy, enable 4-bit quantized variant for low-priority routes, aggressive batching for background rerank jobs routed only to Dedicated.

Unresolved tradeoffs / discussion notes: 
- How long to keep bridgehead in place after cutover? Ops prefers 30 days. Customer security team prefers shorter (7–14) to reduce attack surface. Need agreement.
- Should the bridgehead do partial KV caching for prefixes from Hosted to reduce duplicated work when routing between variants? Pros: latency wins. Cons: consistency complexity and cache invalidation across envs.
- Model variant parity: can we ensure private environment supports identical optimized kernels (quantized) used in Hosted? If not, we must maintain a compatibility mapping and explicit regression tests.

Runbook checklist (Stage A -> C):
- Pre-stage tasks (owner: Maya): NDA complete, baseline data export (sample prompts), Confluence pre-read shared.
- Stage A (owner: Liam): deploy hosted pinned model, enable detailed token/logging flags, run 2-week traffic capture; collect latency percentiles and token histogram. Jira: ENG-4021.
- Stage B (owner: Sofia): create bridgehead infra (terraform module: bridgehead-lite), configure routing policy, deploy Dedicated pool minimal commit, run 48h split-test. Create dashboards and SLO alerts. Jira: ENG-4098.
- Stage C (owner: Rajiv): complete VPC peering and KMS access window, run compliance checklist, flip traffic routing incrementally over 2 maintenance windows. Decommission bridgehead after agreed observation window. Jira: ENG-4150.

Metrics to validate success:
- Functional: 99th p99 latency < 250ms for generation endpoints (goal <150ms), model output similarity within X% (eval set), error rate < 0.5%.
- Business: Cost per 1k tokens within target budget, fewer than 2 rollback events during canary.

Action items (short):
- Maya: draft external-facing onboarding checklist for customer; due 2026-02-27. (TO DO: link to Confluence draft)
- Liam: instrument hosted experiment flags to include model-hash tag; ENG-4021; due 2026-02-23.
- Sofia: deliver terraform bridgehead-lite module and example vars; PR-4893; due 2026-03-05.
- Rajiv: validate kernel parity matrix with runtime team and list lacking op kernels; ENG-4150; due 2026-02-28.

Notes to self / rough ideas: 
- Consider a 'slow-path' endpoint on Dedicated that always uses quantized model and a 'fast-path' on Hosted that uses non-quantized for low-latency but higher cost. Bridgehead can map user-tier flag -> route.
- Automate periodic drift checks between Hosted and Private model outputs using small evaluation prompts; fail canary if divergence > threshold.

Appendix (links & refs):
- Short demo script for customer call: steps to flip 10% route -> 50% -> 90% -> 100%; checklist of rollback commands and metrics to watch.
- Related internal docs: "model-onboarding-checklist" (Confluence), "dedicated-reservation-guidelines" (SE playbook).

Open questions for next sync:
- Customer legal: acceptable bridgehead retention period? (owner: Maya)
- Infra: acceptable default autoscale thresholds for Dedicated pools during split tests? (owner: Sofia)

End of doc.
